title: Sri Krishna's Hunger
body:
Sri Krishna's Hunger

ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ।।

"In whatever way people surrender unto me, I reciprocate with them accordingly. Everyone follows my path, knowingly or unknowingly, O son of Pritha. (Gita IV-11)"

Back in Hastinapur, Duryodhana performed the Vaishnava sacrifice with great pomp, hosting the volatile Sage Durvasa and his ten thousand disciples. Durvasa, highly pleased with Duryodhana's lavish hospitality, offered him a boon. Duryodhana, conspiring to bring about the destruction of the Pandavas, requested Durvasa to visit his brothers in the forest, suggesting a specific time when he knew they would have finished their meal and no food would be left in their hermitage.
Durvasa arrived at the Pandavas' hermitage just after Draupadi had cleaned the Akshayapatra (the vessel of inexhaustible food given by the Sun God), ending its power for the day. Facing the prospect of a devastating curse from the irritable sage for their lack of hospitality, Draupadi prayed fervently to Lord Krishna in her distress.
Lord Krishna appeared instantly, declaring: 'I am exceedingly hungry; bring me something to eat first!' Draupadi cried out in confusion, pointing to the empty vessel. Krishna inspected the pot, found a single grain of rice sticking to the rim, and consumed it with satisfaction. In that instant, Durvasa and his ten thousand disciples, who were bathing in the river, felt their stomachs swell with complete, pleased satiety. They felt as if they had consumed a royal feast, and fearing they could not eat a single bite of the food prepared by Yudhishthira, they quietly departed. This beautiful episode demonstrates that when the Supreme Soul is satisfied, the entire universe is satisfied.
